newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM sells Northwest stake, strengthens link.
newsitem.headline: KLM sells Northwest stake, strengthens link.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Wednesday it would sell its shares in Northwest Airlines, but would strengthen its operational alliance with the U.S. carrier.
"KLM and its U.S. partner Northwest Airlines have agreed in principle on a far-reaching and long-term commercial and operational alliance," the airlines said in a joint statement.

"The agreement in principle also includes the sale of the entire KLM stake in Northwest to Northwest Airlines Corporation (NWAC). KLM will be paid a minimum of USD 1.07 billion and a maximum of USD 1.7 billion," the statement said.

"The agreement clears the way for further strengthening of the partnership, which continues to be very successful for both companies. It may lead to what may well be the most far-reaching airline alliance ever seen in the globalising airline industry."
KLM's stake of about 19 percent in Northwest will be sold off in four annual tranches from 1997 to 2000.
The two airlines have agreed to appoint one member to each other's board and to commit themselves for a minimum of 10 years to a commercial and operational partnership.
They said they would pursue further widening of their alliance through the addition of new partners.
They also plan to intensify cooperation in the air freight sector.
